transcript:
Header: 2026-08-18 16:00 PDT | Duration: 47m | Recording: Yes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood CSM); Alex (Solace DS), Priya (Solace Security), Miguel (Solace PM), QA (Speaker 1)

Summary: quick sync on the quality eval we ran with the expanded prompt set, walked through top regression buckets and agreed on next steps (share prompts, run larger regression, schedule perf run).

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call?
[00:05] Alex: alex here, miguel and priya also on my side.
[00:10] Maya: maya from redwood, hi all.
[00:12] Miguel: miguel, product.
[00:15] Priya: priya, security.
[00:18] Speaker 1: QA here.

[00:23] Jordan: cool, so agenda today: we'll run through last week's quality eval results, the regression check outputs, and then discuss guardrails and next steps. maya you wanna lead the results?
[00:30] Maya: yeah for sure. quick note — the transcription on the export might show 'Redwood Dedicate' in places, small autopct typo. ok, so we evaluated 250 test prompts against the tuned prompt set A and baseline prompt set B, scoring on a 0-100 rubric that we shared last friday.

[00:48] Alex: just to clarify, that rubric is the mix of precision/recall for entity extraction plus a clinical-safety penalty, right?
[00:53] Maya: yup exactly. weightings: 50% extraction accuracy, 30% clinical safety (hallucination penalty), 20% formatting/response completeness. we used automated checkers plus a small human review sample (n=30).

[01:15] Speaker 1: i noticed the human review flagged a few formatting regressions where the model omitted the units — like mg/dl.
[01:20] Maya: yep that's one of the top buckets. ok so high level: prompt A improved average score from 72 to 81 versus baseline, so net +9 points. we saw improvements on entity recall and reduced hallucinations in free-text summarization.

[01:42] Miguel: that's great, what's the distribution though? any big outliers?
[01:45] Maya: good question. the distribution is skewed — most cases improved, but ~12% regressed by >10 points. those regressions fall into three main buckets: unit omission (formatting), over-trimming of explanation (response truncated), and a small set of edge-case lab descriptions where the model invented values.

[02:10] Alex: can you show an example of the invented-values case?
[02:15] Maya: sure. here's a sample — source: patient note mentions 'sodium slightly low'; baseline and tuned both list sodium, but tuned added a numeric like '138 mmol/L' where the note had none. so that's a hallucination introduced by a prompt expansion that encouraged generating concise numeric summaries.

[02:40] Jordan: that one is concerning for clinical safety obviously. priya, any initial flags from security/compliance?
[02:45] Priya: yeah our immediate concern is auditability — we need deterministic traceability why a number was synthesized. also want to ensure we can disable numeric inference with a guardrail. do you have options for builders to turn off 'numeric completion'?
[02:58] Maya: we do — we can add a guardrail in the prompt pipeline and at the routing level. two approaches: 1) prompt-level instruction to not synthesize values and prefer 'not specified' or 2) post-process detector that strips clinically-inferred numbers and flags for human review. both are possible.

[03:20] Alex: which is easier to roll into the POC quickly?
[03:22] Maya: prompt change is fastest to iterate on. detector needs ~2-3 days to tune thresholds to avoid false positives.

[03:30] Jordan: ok action: maya to push a revised prompt that includes the numeric-suppression guardrail; jordan will send to alex.

[03:36] Speaker 1: can we add a quick unit-check post-process too? that's what caused the mg/dl omission issues.
[03:42] Maya: yes — we'll add a 'units required' check that raises low-confidence responses. that's a small post-processing rule.

[03:50] Miguel: what about the truncation / over-trimming bucket? sometimes the tuned prompt is too concise.
[03:55] Maya: that's likely from an aggressive 'be concise' instruction we added. we can relax the brevity parameter for summaries or add a minimum token requirement. also we saw a few timeouts when the model hit the 512 token cut, so we should profile seq length.

[04:18] Jordan: speaking of profiling, we ran some initial latency/cost numbers last week on hosted vs dedicated configurations — i put a note in the shared sheet. do we need to schedule a proper benchmark?

[04:28] Alex: yes, we want end-to-end p99 latency numbers with the full pipeline (prompt, kv cache hit/miss, post-process). ideally run both hosted and dedicated to compare.

[04:35] Maya: i'll spin up a reproducible notebook that hits the same 250 prompts and captures token counts, p50/p95/p99, and cost per 1k tokens. that should be ready by monday.

[04:45] Alex: perfect. also, for regression monitoring long-term, what's your suggestion for an automated alert when new commits drop quality?

[04:52] Maya: we have a Redwood Optimize hook — you can push baseline tests into the evals pipeline and get regression alerts by prompt set. we can demo that in the console. right now it's configured for the POC test suite but we can add thresholds and webhook alerts to your Slack or JIRA.

[05:10] Priya: on security: we received the SOC2 excerpt you sent; thanks. a couple asks: KMS/HSM for keys, audit logs retention 1 year minimum, and SSO via SAML with SCIM provisioning. can Redwood support these in a Private deployment?

[05:25] Jordan: yes on paper — Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and extended audit retention; SSO + SCIM is standard for enterprise. we'll put together a short doc mapping capabilities to your asks.

[05:36] Priya: and for the pilot, we need to know what is logged — are prompts persisted? where do logs live?

[05:42] Liam: quick answer — by default hosted logs are retained per our standard retention policy, but for dedicated/private you can turn off prompt retention and enable redaction. we'll follow up with the exact retention windows and redaction controls.

[05:58] Alex: coming back to the regression failures — is there a way to triage them by root cause automatically? like labeling whether it's prompt, model, or postprocess?

[06:05] Maya: we annotate failures with heuristics: token-level diffs, hallucination detector, and formatting checks. that auto-label covers about 70% of failures; the remainder need a quick human triage. we can add a column to the failure CSV with the heuristic label.

[06:25] Speaker 1: can we see the failure CSV now?
[06:27] Maya: yes i uploaded a CSV to the shared drive — link in the chat: https://redwood.ai/poc/solacedx/failures-20260818.csv (note: placeholder link).

[06:40] Miguel: ok i pulled it — looks like 31 failing rows flagged 'formatting' and 18 'hallucination'. we'd like to prioritize hallucination fixes first.
[06:50] Jordan: agreed. so prioritization: 1) numeric hallucination guardrail (prompt + detector), 2) units/formatting post-process, 3) response-length adjustments, 4) run larger regression.

[07:05] Alex: timeline?

[07:07] Jordan: maya will ship prompt + small post-process by Friday (2026-08-20). alex runs regression by Tuesday (2026-08-25). maya will run perf benchmarks and share results Monday (2026-08-24). priya to confirm security requirements by 2026-08-21.

[07:25] Priya: one more security note — for the audit logs, we need proof of tamper-resistance and the ability to export logs to our SIEM.

[07:32] Liam: we support export to S3 or streaming to your SIEM; we'll include the export pattern in the follow-up doc.

[07:40] Speaker 1: any blockers on our side?

[07:42] Alex: dev bandwidth — we'll prioritize the regression runs but might need a quick script from redwood to normalize results.

[07:48] Maya: we'll provide the notebook and a small wrapper script to run locally.

[07:54] Jordan: ok let's do a quick recap of action items…
[08:00] Jordan: maya to send revised prompt + post-process rules; jordan to share scoring rubric; maya to provide perf notebook; alex to run regression; priya to share KMS/HSM details.

[08:12] Miguel: scheduling — can we do the perf benchmark on thursday?

[08:15] Maya: thursday works, i'll confirm times after posting the notebook.

[08:20] Jordan: last thing — any competitor mentions or concerns?

[08:23] Alex: someone on the team tried Anthropic for a small subset and saw slightly fewer hallucinations but higher cost; we still want to compare p99 and cost per 1k tokens.

[08:34] Jordan: great — we'll include OpenAI and Anthropic baseline numbers in the perf doc for comparison.

[08:40] Speaker 1: thanks everyone.

[08:42] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up with the doc and prompt set. talk soon.

End of recording.
